text: The US Open has been played on grass, green clay and hard courts. Its hard-court era began in 1978.
The Australian Open switched from grass to hard courts when it moved to Flinders Park, now Melbourne Park, in 1988.
Australian Open courts turned blue in 2008. The hard courts at Melbourne Park had previously been green.
Roland-Garros gets its red colour from a brick-dust layer only about two millimetres thick.
Roland-Garros stadium honours a French aviator: Roland Garros.
Roland-Garros opened in 1928 with just five courts.
Wimbledon's playing grass is trimmed to eight millimetres for The Championships.
Since 2001, Wimbledon's courts have been planted entirely with perennial ryegrass to help them withstand wear.
The first Wimbledon Championships, in 1877, had 22 entrants and only a men's singles competition.
A regulation court is 23.77 metres long. Doubles alleys widen the playing area from 8.23 to 10.97 metres.
The net dips in the middle: its height is 0.914 metres at the centre, compared with 1.07 metres at the posts.
Yellow balls joined the tennis rules in 1972 after research found them easier for television viewers to see.
A ball touching the relevant boundary line counts as in. It does not have to land completely inside the line.
A legal return can travel around a net post and land in the opponent's court; it need not pass above the net.
With advantage scoring, deuce becomes a two-point challenge: win the next two points consecutively to take the game.
